arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Goldstein argued the ADEA embodies Congress' determination against age discrimination.
Mr. Goldstein stated the Act prohibits practices lacking reasonable business justification.
Mr. Nager argued mere statistical correlations do not create a prima facie case.
Justice Breyer questioned the practical application of the business necessity standard.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act. the sides that brought the case argue the law bans practices that harm older workers without business justification. The City argues the statute only bans intentional discrimination. The dispute centers on statutory interpretation and lower court rulings.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the scope of federal age discrimination protections. It determines whether employers face liability for neutral practices that harm older workers. This affects hiring, compensation, and workforce composition decisions nationwide.
